Capabilities and Limitations of Composition-Only Machine Learning for Predicting the Thermodynamic Stability of Multicomponent Zn-, In-, and Sn-Based Oxides¶

Interactive walk-through of the complete pipeline (seed = 42). Each section calls the corresponding script in scripts/, ensuring identical results between the notebook and command-line execution.

Requirements: environment.yml or requirements.txt. Place the archived raw dataset in data/raw/mp_doped_oxides_raw.csv (or set MP_API_KEY and set REFRESH_RAW = True below).

In [1]:
import subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Image, display

# Locate the project root (folder containing environment.yml)
ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "environment.yml").exists())
REFRESH_RAW = False   # Set True to re-query the Materials Project API

def run(script):
    """Run one pipeline script (same env as run_all.py), stream output live, log to logs/steps/."""
    import os
    print(f"\n>>> {script}")
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.update(PYTHONUTF8="1", PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8", JOBLIB_MULTIPROCESSING="0")
    log_dir = ROOT / "logs" / "steps"; log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    log = log_dir / f"nb_{Path(script).stem}.log"
    lines = []
    with open(log, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "scripts" / script)], cwd=ROOT, env=env,
                             stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                             text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", bufsize=1)
        for line in p.stdout:
            print(line, end=""); fh.write(line); lines.append(line)
        p.wait()
    if p.returncode:
        print("".join(lines[-25:]))
        raise RuntimeError(f"{script} failed (code {p.returncode}) - log: {log}")

def show(*patterns):
    for pat in patterns:
        for f in sorted(ROOT.glob(pat)):
            print(f.relative_to(ROOT)); display(Image(filename=f))

print("Project root:", ROOT)

======================================================================
[STEP 3.2] PHYSICAL INTERPRETATION - Feature Families
======================================================================

  * Stoichiometric:
    Compositional complexity - the Lp norms capture how unevenly the 
    constituent elements are distributed across the composition. 
    Compositions close to a binary oxide have higher Lp norms than 
    equimolar multicomponent mixtures (Ward et al., 2016). 

  * Electronic Structure:
    Orbital character - the fraction of s/p/d/f valence electrons encodes 
    whether the compound is dominated by main-group (s/p) or 
    transition-metal (d) bonding. 

  * Ionic Compound:
    Ionic character - the maximum electronegativity difference captures 
    bond polarity and electrostatic stabilization in multicomponent oxides 
    (Hautier et al., 2014).
